text: my company gives me 5 lakh group cover, so why would I pay extra
I'm covered by my employer's group policy, so I don't need my own health insurance.

chain.why: Employer cover belongs to the employer's group policy; the regulator's option to move it into your own name applies only when you leave the group.
A fresh policy bought after leaving a job, rather than migrated, starts its waiting periods from zero.
About 1 in 9 Indian adults aged 20 and over has diabetes, and more than 1 in 3 has high blood pressure.

conclusion: When you leave the employer's group cover and bought a fresh policy, the waiting periods starts from zero and Indian adults have diabetes and high blood pressure.

text: I hear you – you’re wondering why you’d need anything beyond the group cover. Based on IRDAI circular IRDAI/HLT/REG/CIR/003/01/2020, this means the employer’s cover belongs to the group policy and the option to move it into your own name only applies when you exit the group. What would you consider if you changed jobs or left the company?

text: You mentioned your employer’s 5 lakh group cover. Based on IRDAI circular IRDAI/HLT/REG/CIR/003/01/2020, that cover belongs to the group policy and can only be moved to your name when you leave the group; a new individual policy would start its waiting periods from zero (IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business, 29 May 2024), and given that about 1 in 9 Indian adults has diabetes and over 1 in 3 have high blood pressure (ICMR‑INDIAB‑17, Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology, Jul 2023), relying solely on the group cover may leave gaps if you change jobs or develop health issues.
